name: issues_comment
description: Post one comment on an issue in Ledgerline's tracker. It is public: the reporter reads it. Call it once per triage, as the run's last write: after reading the file you will name, and after the pull request when there is one. The body's first two lines must be 'label: <bug | feature | question | docs>' and 'file: <path relative to the repository root, or none>'. The result is JSON {comment, issue}, the new comment's identifier; it is never empty when the comment posted. Safe to retry: the harness keys every write, so a repeat of the same comment returns the first one and posts nothing. Bodies are capped at 2,000 characters; a longer body is an error, not cut.

issue.description: The issue to comment on, such as issue-4192: the one you read.

body.description: At most 2,000 characters: the label line, the file line, then one or two sentences on why that file. A question's file is none.

input.body:
label: bug
file: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The button is never re-enabled when an export fails.

examples.note: the typical call: a bug, with the file the code is wrong in

input.body:
label: question
file: none

The reporter asks how a setting works; nothing needs to change.

examples.note: a hard case: a question names no file, so the file line says none
